tldr: Google DeepMind released a substantial human-guided, machine-checked Signal verification study, while fresh agent-infrastructure, security-fingerprinting, research-review and small-model-learning preprints propose new techniques.

Reports on semiconductor bottlenecks, deep-sea robot trials, UK surveillance funding and French chatbot-regulation proposals broaden the picture; author results, company claims and advisory recommendations remain explicitly qualified.

news.title: DeepMind releases AlphaProof Code proofs for Signal's core cryptography
news.summary: Google DeepMind presented AlphaProof Code, a human-guided multi-agent framework using Lean-checked proof artifacts to connect defined cryptographic guarantees with compiled AArch64 libsignal code, covering PQXDH and Triple Ratchet properties.
news.why_it_matters: A notable demonstration of scaling verification beyond abstract protocol design into executable code.
news.caveat: It does not certify the entire Signal app or unspecified properties. The proofs depend on trusted human-approved specifications, model assumptions and the Lean kernel.

news.title: Evolving Infra proposes workload-adaptive prefill, decode and KV-cache management
news.summary: A November 9 preprint introduces dynamic prefill/decode GPU role switching and context-aware cache retention for agent workloads. Authors report up to 4.1x lower mean latency and 14x lower P95 time-to-first-token than their selected NVIDIA Dynamo setups.
news.why_it_matters: Long-running agent tasks often reuse prefixes after subagent work or pauses that recency-only cache eviction cannot anticipate.
news.caveat: These are unreplicated preprint maxima on selected workloads with up to 256 GB300 GPUs; a downloadable release was not verified.

news.title: Shibboleth research fingerprints attacking agent models and harnesses
news.summary: Researchers describe honeypot services that elicit characteristic language, command timeouts and tool-call behavior from an autonomous attacker. In controlled experiments they report 90% top-1 model classification across 15 candidates and 92% harness identification across four harnesses.
news.why_it_matters: Defenders may infer which tools or models drive an attack without direct access to the attacker's prompts or agent logs.
news.caveat: Controlled testing is not evidence of a real incident or universal attribution; the linked code repository was empty when checked.

news.title: PARIS research proposes a human-gated agent workflow for systematic reviews
news.summary: The PARIS preprint describes specialized review agents coordinated through persisted artifacts, three human checkpoints and a pre-synthesis corpus-quality measure. Two case studies reveal both useful workflows and retrieval/count-tracking failures.
news.why_it_matters: Auditable study selection and human oversight matter more than presenting an AI-generated research summary as a completed systematic review.
news.caveat: Unreviewed preprint: only eight of 27 PRISMA items fully supported, manuscripts judged internally, and the referenced public repository returned 404.

news.title: SCALE tests small-model-first learning from selectively triggered LLM reflection
news.summary: A November 9 preprint proposes a small model for routine agent decisions, using larger-model reflection on failures to create reusable conceptual knowledge and archive old experiences.
news.why_it_matters: Selectively internalizing experience could reduce recurring large-model calls in long-running agents.
news.caveat: Author-controlled experiments only; model generalization, deployed resource costs and independent reproducibility remain unverified.

technologies.name: AlphaProof Code
technologies.explanation: Human-guided Gemini-backed agents draft formal specifications and multi-agent proofs, checked by Lean against approved statements and modeled compiled AArch64 code.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Can dramatically reduce manual proof generation where trusted specifications and expert reviewers already exist.
tradeoffs: A verified theorem addresses only its stated properties
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: The case study uses proprietary large models, Lean and AArch64 semantics; no minimum supported runtime for the full agent pipeline was verified.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Proof artifacts public; complete reusable framework license not established.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Research write-up and proofs accessible; no supported general-purpose product release verified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Undisclosed model usage and compute costs.

technologies.name: Evolving Infra
technologies.explanation: Decouples prefill-decode compute reallocation from context-aware distributed KV-cache retention for dynamic agent workloads.
technologies.conditional_advantage: May lower latency in large clusters with fluctuating prefill/decode demand and long-lived agent prompt prefixes.
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Evaluated on up to 256 GB300 GPUs; local laptop or low-cost runtime not demonstrated.
technologies.license_uncertainty: Paper published; executable project license not verified.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: No independent runnable public project release confirmed.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Requires substantial GPU cluster infrastructure; costs unverified.

technologies.name: PARIS (PRISMA Agentic Research Intelligence System)
technologies.explanation: A Claude Code conductor coordinates specialized review agents and persisted, audited research artifacts, with human checkpoints before literature synthesis.
technologies.conditional_advantage: Can structure auditable review stages when a domain expert verifies inclusion, corpus quality and conclusions.
tradeoffs: Retrieval incompleteness and count drift in authors' tests
technologies.hardware_runtime_constraints: Paper describes Claude Code, Python data-science packages, Jupyter and document export tools; API/model consumption may cost money.
technologies.license_uncertainty: MIT license is claimed in preprint but repository returned 404.
technologies.availability_uncertainty: Authors' named GitHub repo did not open; installability unverified.
technologies.pricing_uncertainty: Potential Claude/API charges; no product price independently verified.

terms.name: Shibboleth trap
terms.definition: A purpose-built honeypot service that draws out model- or tool-harness-specific behavior from an autonomous agent interacting with a defended target.
terms.mechanism: Controlled interaction gates can elicit writing style, masking behavior, timeout handling or tool-call scheduling patterns.
terms.example: An agent seeking a credential is required to write a change record; a defender scores its linguistic and tool-use patterns.
terms.caveat: Statistical identification is not proof of identity; research code repository was empty on check.

terms.name: Agent-aware KV-cache retention
terms.definition: A cache-retention policy using an agent's execution state to predict when past attention key/value prefixes will be reused.
terms.mechanism: Subagent branches, context compaction and likely future resumptions inform eviction decisions rather than access recency alone.
terms.example: A paused subagent retains its cached prefix during a long external tool call because it will resume later.
terms.caveat: Can increase memory and communication costs, and results depend on accurate agent-state telemetry.

terms.name: Machine-code-level formal verification
terms.definition: Mathematical proof that a compiled executable satisfies explicitly defined properties under a model of machine instructions and external assumptions.
terms.mechanism: The binary's execution semantics are encoded in a proof assistant, and its behavior is linked to trusted statements checked by a proof kernel.
terms.example: Lean checks a theorem that an AArch64 libsignal binary meets stated post-compromise security conditions.
terms.caveat: A proof is only as broad as the specification, instruction semantics and assumptions; it does not imply an application has no bugs.
